provenance.paper_title: VideoAgent: A Memory-augmented Multimodal Agent for Video Understanding

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: Segment captions, caption embeddings, and time positions form temporal memory; tools retrieve captions by time or semantic relevance.

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: Each video segment has a visual feature used for query-to-segment localization, with the segment identity retained.

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: Re-identified objects are stored in a feature table and SQL database with categories and temporal appearances; an LLM tool generates database queries.

representation_paths.memory_component: raw video available to VQA tool

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: After localizing a segment from memory, the agent can invoke visual question answering on the corresponding raw video segment.

derived.hybrid_relation: Source-linked captions, visual features, relational object state, and recoverable video segments are jointly routed by tools.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 6): The full-paper lifecycle review found temporal memory fixed during downstream inference; query-conditioned access, preprocessing, or training-time changes were not counted as persistent deployed updates. No persistent inference-time T2 update or deployment-feedback policy evolution was found.
